summary.headline: Hariom Pipe Q2 FY27 revenue rose 65% YoY to INR 554 crore and PAT to INR 29 crore, with EBITDA per tonne at INR 8,140.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations rose 65% YoY to INR 554 crore, EBITDA rose 58% to INR 68 crore and PAT rose to INR 29 crore from INR 10 crore, with EBITDA margin at 12.21%. Management attributed the recovery to the Perundurai unit restarting on July 13 after a roughly 110-day closure in Q1. H1 revenue was INR 983 crore (up 23%), EBITDA INR 118 crore (up 17%) and PAT INR 46 crore (up 35%). Management guided to 10-15% growth for H2 FY27 and FY28 and a 25% volume growth base case, while the solar portfolio and Andhra Pradesh steel MOU remain early-stage.

segments.name: Steel (standalone) volumes
segments.commentary: Q2 sales volume was 83,117 tonnes, up 32% QoQ; H1 volume was about 1.46 lakh tonnes, up 6% YoY. Q2 split: integrated steel plant ~29,000 t, Mahbubnagar galvanised ~29,600 t, Perundurai ~23,400-24,000 t, Anantapur sponge iron ~1,000 t.

segments.name: Hariom Power and Energy (solar)
segments.commentary: 15 MWac is operational across three locations after 5 MWac in July and two 5 MWac projects in October (the latter after the half-year end). Portfolio is 60 MW across 13 locations in Maharashtra; target is 52 MW across 11 locations by January 2027.

segments.name: Metal Mart (trading subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Completed documentation and obtained GST registration in H1; fuller operations are planned for the current quarter. No revenue contribution was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27: minimum 10-15% growth from current run-rate, per Managing Director.
FY28: management expects 10-15% growth again, with acquisitions and brownfield expansion under evaluation; projections may rise from the next or the quarter after.
Volume growth: management's stated target is not less than 25% a year (earlier 30%); 25% was described as the base case for FY28, with acquisitions as upside.
EBITDA margin: management said it is consistently above 12%; if the proposed HR coil/integrated capacity is built, EBITDA could rise to 13-15%.
Long-term vision: INR 10,000 crore top line within 5-6 years, per the MD.

Solar: 52 MW across 11 locations targeted by January 2027. Management expects roughly INR 28-30 crore revenue and INR 3-4 crore net surplus after debt, depreciation and interest once 52 MW is operational, over 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Total steel capacity is 5,21,000 tonnes of finished goods. Breakdown: Perundurai 1,80,000 t; Mahbubnagar galvanised 1,20,000 t; the remaining ~2,21,000 t is integrated steel plant output.

Maharashtra capex announced for a large steel expansion; the MOU is about 1.5 years old and still facing issues. Management expects execution over 3-4 years and plans an HR coil unit with backward integration, but gave no timeline or quantum.
Andhra Pradesh integrated steel plant MOU is non-binding, subject to due diligence, approvals and land allocation. It would be built within existing land at the current facility.
Perundurai: 4 MW DC of solar power under an MOU, which management said will lower power costs. Operations resumed July 13, 2026 after the Q1 closure.
Solar: 52 MW out of 60 MW awarded is targeted. Two sites face land scarcity and the alternative substation request is pending; if not granted, the build is capped at 52 MW.
demand_pricing: Management said about 20% of Q2 volume (~83,000 t) came from OEM customers. Focus is on OEM and value-added products, which carry better margins than standard galvanised or cold-rolled pipe.
Management said a single customer is no more than 5-6% of revenue, and about 80% of sales go through dealers with the balance direct B2B. The company has more than 800 SKUs.
Q2 EBITDA per tonne rise was attributed to lower fixed cost at Perundurai after full operation, higher integrated-steel margins, better market absorption and power and opex efficiency.
Power consumption per tonne fell to about 98 units in Q2 from about 135 units in Q1, per management.

Power and fuel expense rose to about INR 25 crore in Q2 from about INR 18 crore in Q1. Management cited restart costs, higher Mahbubnagar galvanised utilisation, and higher tariffs and additional charges. Electricity is the major component of power cost.
Management said peak revenue at the 5.21 lakh t capacity could be about INR 2,500-2,800 crore at present steel prices, depending on market conditions.

qa_highlights.question: What are H2 FY27 and FY28 growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: MD guided minimum 10-15% growth for H2 FY27 and 10-15% again for FY28. The CFO declined to give a specific number at first, and management said EBITDA per tonne and margins should hold.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume growth target and is 25% a base case?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the target is at least 25% volume growth (earlier 30%). Management said 25% is the base case for FY28, with acquisitions as upside.

qa_highlights.question: How will the planned steel capex be funded and what margin impact is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Maharashtra project will take 3-4 years, with an HR coil unit planned for backward integration. EBITDA margin could rise from 12% to 13-15% if it is built. No funding plan was specified.

qa_highlights.question: Is GP pipe and coil dependence a concentration risk and what is the water-security position?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said GP segment growth reflects new customers and geographies. The company is not affected by the Hyderabad water situation.

qa_highlights.question: Solar subsidiary revenue and surplus from the 60 MW portfolio?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said 52 MW would generate about INR 28-30 crore of top line and INR 3-4 crore net surplus over 4-5 years after debt, depreciation and interest. Power from Maharashtra plants goes to MSEDCL under PM-KUSUM and cannot be used for manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the power cost increase and what is the Tamil Nadu power arrangement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher production, Perundurai running on units rather than minimum demand charges, and extra tariff charges. A 25-year PPA-style MOU with a solar company supplies about 4 MW DC for Perundurai. Electricity is the main power cost component.

qa_highlights.question: What is the vision and expansion strategy beyond FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD set a goal of INR 10,000 crore top line in 5-6 years and said acquisitions, franchising models and brownfield expansion are under evaluation. Management said there are no finalised deals, and the Andhra Pradesh MOU is non-binding.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the Maharashtra steel expansion and the Andhra Pradesh MOU, which is non-binding and subject to approvals and land allocation.
Solar: two sites are short of land and the substation approval is pending, which may cap capacity at 52 MW out of 60 MW awarded.
Power cost pressure: power and fuel costs rose to about INR 25 crore in Q2 from INR 18 crore in Q1, and management attributed this partly to tariff additions.
Concentration: GP pipes and coils dependence is rising, per an analyst. Single-customer exposure is capped at 5-6%.
Working capital and inventory rise from holding more than 800 SKUs, with 8-9 SKUs per dealer lot.
Tamil Nadu pollution-control issue: management said operations are normal, but no detail on cost or permit timing was provided.
Promoter warrant issue at INR 333 per warrant, with 25% margin money received. Management said the funds are for expansion and capital needs.
Management did not quantify the H2 volume target, the FY28 volume target or the HR coil capex amount, and gave no funding plan for the expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q2 recovery and near-term growth, but noticeably vague on specific numbers. Management repeatedly declined to quantify FY28, capex, the funding plan and the Andhra Pradesh project, and cited factors "not in our hands". Tone was defensive on the solar investment and the Tamil Nadu shutdown.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin was 12.21% in Q2 vs 11.63% in Q1 and management says it is consistently above 12%, but a 13-15% margin depends on building the unfunded HR coil capacity, which has no timeline.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Solar capacity is coming live (15 MWac operational, 52 MW targeted by January 2027), but the steel expansions are only planned: Maharashtra HR coil has no timeline or quantum and the Andhra Pradesh MOU is non-binding.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides volume growth of not less than 25% a year, with Q2 volume at 83,117 t up 32% QoQ and the Perundurai restart on July 13, though H1 volume was only up 6% YoY and no H2 volume number was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: The Maharashtra HR coil unit is planned with backward integration and the Andhra Pradesh MOU is under evaluation; the company has ~2.21 lakh t of integrated output and 1.8 lakh t Perundurai, but utilisation was not disclosed, so the call is based on stated plans rather than a utilisation read.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is a minimum of 10-15% growth for H2 FY27 and FY28, which is modest against Q2 revenue up 65% YoY, and management gave no upgrade and declined to quantify numbers.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Power and fuel costs rose to about INR 25 crore in Q2 from INR 18 crore in Q1, solar sites face land scarcity that may cap capacity at 52 MW of 60 MW, and the Tamil Nadu pollution-control issue has no cost or permit timing.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Focus is on OEM and value-added products with ~20% of Q2 volume (~83,000 t) from OEMs, but no specific new product or launch date was named.

rows.label: OEM and value-added mix shift
rows.why: About 20% of Q2 volume (~83,000 t) came from OEM customers, and management says these carry better margins than standard galvanised or cold-rolled pipe.

rows.label: Power consumption per tonne down
rows.why: Power use fell to about 98 units per tonne in Q2 from about 135 in Q1, and Q2 EBITDA per tonne rose 15% YoY to INR 8,140.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Q2 Perundurai recovery, 25% volume target and 10-15% growth guide, but declined to quantify FY28, capex, funding and the Andhra Pradesh project; analysts pushed on guidance numbers, power costs, the solar build and GP concentration.
